searchText: thanks perema!! it's great, yes this is the kind of format I was looking for did you use any available script or scraped it yourself? haven't found time to dive into ethereum-etl Bit of a naive question, but will "old-style" transactions still be accepted after 1559 is rolled out? The EIP says it's a new transaction type, so I would expect it to be so, but how would it work for the old transactions? Is the gas price automatically split into fee+tip? Yes, legacy transactions will continue to be accepted and propagated around the network and included in blocks. The `gasPrice` in a legacy transaction will be used to cover the base fee, and any remaining amount will go to the miner. Thanks! Then as a followup question: what's the rationale with introducing a new transaction type, couldn't we have kept the old version and done this automatically? Thinking about it, I guess the point is bounding the fee separately from the tip, but is that something that is interesting to toy with at all? Then you wouldn't get any of the UX benefits of 1559, and you wouldn't get good price discovery,. yes, on this point, this is a simulation of legacy users on a 1559 network, with a basefee: https://ethereum.github.io/abm1559/notebooks/transition1559.html#subsec-3-2 in a few cases the basefee is completely irrelevant (~ zero), even though the market rate is positive I'm probably missing something basic. If basefee = 5, and a legacy user sets gasPrice = 10, isn't that identical to setting maxFeePerGas = basefee & maxTipPerGas = 10 - basefee? Isn't that only for "legacy clients" that can't read the base fee from the block? Could we have clients that can read the base fee, but send old-style transactions? It is equivalent to the user setting `maxFee = priorityFee = gasPrice`. Wallets are generally what generate signed transactions, and they can generate/submit either legacy or 1559 transactions. Wait - legacy has `gasPrice` , while EIP-1559 has `priorityFee` & `baseFee` , right? How is your equations possible - it's like you're paying double? (To clarify I interpreted the equations as `maxFeePerGas = maxPriorityFeePerGas = gasPrice`) A legacy transaction with `gasPrice` of `x` is equivalent to a 1559 transaction with a `maxFee` of `x` and a `maxPriorityFee` of `x`. I synced an archive goerli node and then used python `requests` to call `eth_getBlock` over `localhost:8545`. I parsed in batches, populating a comma-separated string for each transaction and then appended to a `xyz.csv` file (first writing header names). The run time for the script was a few minutes. I can do any other sort of data including traces, (for mainnet or goerli) or share the script if you want Ah I see, so my mistake was to assume that in an EIP-1559 you pay (at worst) `(maxFee + maxPriorityFee) * gasConsumed`, it seems to be instead `maxFee * gasConsumed` where `maxPriorityFee` is the portion of the `maxFee` that can be allocated to tips. Is that right? Thanks a lot 🙏

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content: Bit of a naive question, but will "old-style" transactions still be accepted after 1559 is rolled out? The EIP says it's a new transaction type, so I would expect it to be so, but how would it work for the old transactions? Is the gas price automatically split into fee+tip?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Yes, legacy transactions will continue to be accepted and propagated around the network and included in blocks.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The `gasPrice` in a legacy transaction will be used to cover the base fee, and any remaining amount will go to the miner.

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content: Thanks! Then as a followup question: what's the rationale with introducing a new transaction type, couldn't we have kept the old version and done this automatically? Thinking about it, I guess the point is bounding the fee separately from the tip, but is that something that is interesting to toy with at all?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Then you wouldn't get any of the UX benefits of 1559, and you wouldn't get good price discovery,.

excerpts.author: barnabemonnot
excerpts.content:
yes, on this point, this is a simulation of legacy users on a 1559 network, with a basefee: https://ethereum.github.io/abm1559/notebooks/transition1559.html#subsec-3-2

in a few cases the basefee is completely irrelevant (~ zero), even though the market rate is positive

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content:
I'm probably missing something basic.
If basefee = 5, and a legacy user sets gasPrice = 10, isn't that identical to setting maxFeePerGas = basefee & maxTipPerGas = 10 - basefee?

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content: Isn't that only for "legacy clients" that can't read the base fee from the block? Could we have clients that can read the base fee, but send old-style transactions?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It is equivalent to the user setting `maxFee = priorityFee = gasPrice`.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Wallets are generally what generate signed transactions, and they can generate/submit either legacy or 1559 transactions.

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content:
Wait - legacy has `gasPrice` , while EIP-1559 has `priorityFee`  & `baseFee` , right?
How is your equations possible - it's like you're paying double?

excerpts.author: norswap
excerpts.content: (To clarify I interpreted the equations as `maxFeePerGas = maxPriorityFeePerGas = gasPrice`)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: A legacy transaction with `gasPrice` of `x` is equivalent to a 1559 transaction with a `maxFee` of `x` and a `maxPriorityFee` of `x`.
